name: Costa Cruises
signature: Year-round Western Mediterranean 7-night loops, plus Caribbean, Canaries, South America and Asia seasons
intro: Costa brings an Italian sense of occasion to a genuinely worldwide programme — 631 itineraries and 1,280 departures on sale for July 2026 – June 2027 — best sold to GCC clients as a fly-cruise product.
description: Costa Cruises operates nine recently renovated ships, all Italian-flagged, spanning the Western and Eastern Mediterranean, Northern Europe and the fjords, the Caribbean and Antilles, the Canaries, South America, Asia and a round-the-world voyage bookable by segment. Expect generous dining, lively evening entertainment and a ship that feels like a floating piazza, with family, honeymoon and accessibility programmes built into the core offer.

Costa is a fly-cruise for GCC clients, and an easy one: its home ports cluster in the Western Mediterranean at Barcelona, Rome (Civitavecchia), Savona and Marseille, in the Eastern Mediterranean at Venice and Athens, and in Northern Europe at Hamburg, Kiel and Copenhagen — all a one-stop flight from the Gulf. As a Preferred Sales Agent, we hold fares and allocation across the programme and build the flight and pre-cruise hotel into a single booking.

A genuinely worldwide programme: Mediterranean, Northern Europe, Caribbean, Canaries, South America, Asia and a round-the-world voyage bookable in segments

faqs.q: How do GCC clients join a Costa sailing?
faqs.a: As a fly-cruise into one of Costa's home ports. The Western Mediterranean runs year-round from Barcelona, Rome (Civitavecchia), Savona and Marseille; the Eastern Mediterranean from Venice and Athens; and a summer Northern Europe season from Hamburg, Kiel and Copenhagen. We package the flight, the pre-cruise hotel and the sailing as one booking.

faqs.q: Which Costa ships suit a first-time GCC cruise client?
faqs.a: Costa Smeralda and Costa Toscana are the newest, most premium ships in the fleet — both LNG-powered, with extensive family facilities and a customisable in-suite minibar option.

faqs.q: Is Costa a good fit for family bookings?
faqs.a: Yes. Costa promotes dedicated family deals, multi-generational cabin options and an accessibility programme ('Cruises for Everyone'), alongside strong value for multi-cabin bookings.

faqs.q: What's included for suite guests?
faqs.a: Suite guests fleet-wide receive a personal butler, a welcome bottle of Ferrari sparkling wine and an in-suite coffee machine; on Costa Toscana and Costa Smeralda a customisable minibar is also included.

faqs.q: Can a Costa cruise be combined with a Dubai stopover?
faqs.a: Yes — since Costa's Mediterranean and Northern Europe seasons require a flight from the Gulf, we typically build in a Dubai or Abu Dhabi stay either side of the cruise as part of the same booking.

faqs.q: Does Costa offer a round-the-world cruise?
faqs.a: Yes, on Costa Deliziosa and Costa Serena, bookable as a full voyage or as individual segments — useful for clients who want a taste of the World Cruise without the full multi-month commitment.

name: Norwegian Cruise Line
signature: Year-round Caribbean and weekly Hawaii sailings, plus Alaska, Mediterranean and Northern Europe seasons
intro: Norwegian's Freestyle Cruising philosophy — no fixed dining times, no dress codes — spans 785 sailings across 20 regions on sale as at July 2026, making it one of the most requested lines among our GCC agent network.
description: Norwegian Cruise Line operates 21 ships across the Prima, Breakaway Plus, Breakaway, Epic, Jewel, Dawn and Sun classes, with guests choosing their own dining times and dress code fleet-wide. The line sails a genuinely worldwide programme — Caribbean, Bahamas, Bermuda, Mediterranean, Northern Europe, Alaska, Hawaii, Asia, Panama Canal, Mexican Riviera, Australia & New Zealand and more — with The Haven, Studios for solo travellers and family-connecting staterooms covering most traveller types.

One voyage brings clients home the scenic way: a 21-day Norwegian Sun sailing from Athens calls Muscat, Doha and Abu Dhabi before finishing in Dubai, in September 2027. Everything else is fly-cruise, with Dubai an official NCL hotel-package city. As Preferred Sales Agent, we hold fares and group allocations across the worldwide programme.

21 ships sailing a genuinely worldwide programme, from the Caribbean to Asia and Australia
A 21-day Athens–Dubai voyage on Norwegian Sun, calling Muscat, Doha and Abu Dhabi on the way home

faqs.q: Does Norwegian Cruise Line sail from Dubai?
faqs.a: There are no NCL sailings departing from Dubai or any Gulf port. However, select one-way voyages on sale end in the region: a 21-day Mediterranean voyage from Athens on Norwegian Sun finishes via Doha and Abu Dhabi in Dubai, and an 18-day Athens voyage on Norwegian Sky ends in Muscat after Red Sea calls at Aqaba and Jeddah. Otherwise NCL is a fly-cruise product for GCC clients, with Dubai an official hotel-package city.

faqs.q: What is Freestyle Cruising?
faqs.a: NCL's signature approach: no assigned dining times or tables, no formal dress codes, and up to 28 speciality and complimentary dining options fleet-wide.

faqs.q: How many ships does Norwegian operate?
faqs.a: 22, spanning the Prima, Breakaway Plus, Breakaway, Epic, Jewel, Dawn and Sun classes, plus the US-flagged Pride of America.

faqs.q: Can we combine a Dubai stay with an NCL cruise?
faqs.a: Yes — Dubai's Hilton Al Habtoor City is NCL's official partner hotel for pre- or post-cruise stays connecting into Asia sailings (Singapore, Tokyo, Bangkok, Seoul, Taipei, Manila, Kuala Lumpur) or other Extraordinary Journeys embarkation ports.

faqs.q: Which ship or cabin type suits a solo traveller?
faqs.a: NCL's Studios are purpose-built single-occupancy cabins with access to an exclusive private lounge, available across several ships in the fleet.

faqs.q: Does Norwegian suit large or multi-generational families?
faqs.a: Yes — The Haven offers a private, butler-served enclave, alongside larger connecting family staterooms across the wider fleet.

name: Elixir Cruises
tagline: A boutique two-yacht line in the Greek islands
signature: 7-night boutique yacht voyages through the Cyclades, from Lavrion (Athens), April–October
intro: Elixir is a genuinely small, boutique operation — two named yachts sailing the Greek islands — best suited to GCC clients wanting an intimate, high-touch cruise rather than a mainstream fleet.
description: Elixir Cruises sails two small yachts of its own: Elysium (64 metres, 25 cabins), based in Lavrion for an Aegean season, and M/Y Gemaya, typically sold by individual cabin. The company is headquartered in Ras Al Khaimah in the UAE, with its management office in Piraeus — a rare cruise operator with its own Gulf base.

The product is the Cyclades: week-long round trips from Lavrion (Athens) calling at Mykonos, Santorini, Milos, Sifnos, Naxos and Serifos, with themed departures through the April–October season and one Greece & Turkey itinerary. We wholesale Elixir inventory to our agent network, so you can package it with confidence while being upfront with clients about the boutique scale of the operation.

faqs.q: Where does Elixir sail?
faqs.a: The Cyclades, on week-long round trips from Lavrion (Athens) between April and October — Mykonos, Santorini, Milos, Sifnos, Naxos and Serifos. Elixir is headquartered in Ras Al Khaimah, and Athens is four to five hours from any Gulf hub, so it sells as an easy short-haul fly-cruise.

faqs.q: How big are Elixir's ships?
faqs.a: Elysium carries 50 guests across 25 cabins; Gemaya has just 5 suites and is typically sold by individual cabin rather than full-ship charter.

faqs.q: Is Elixir a good fit for large groups?
faqs.a: Not usually — given the very small scale of both yachts, Elixir suits couples, small groups and bespoke charters rather than large multi-cabin bookings.

faqs.q: What's included in an Elixir fare?
faqs.a: Cabin amenities, buffet breakfast plus half-board dining, a welcome cocktail and non-alcoholic drinks are included on Elysium; Gemaya's fare additionally includes an open bar, port taxes, transfers and water toys.

faqs.q: Can Elixir be booked as a private charter?
faqs.a: Yes — both yachts are used for private charters, incentive groups, honeymoons and small theme cruises alongside their scheduled itineraries.

faqs.q: When does the Elixir season run?
faqs.a: April to October, from Lavrion (Athens). Elixir publishes themed departures across the season — UNESCO heritage, wellness at sea and Greek Easter among them — plus one Greece & Turkey itinerary.

name: Scenic & Emerald Cruises
signature: European river cruising on the Rhine, Danube and Douro, plus yacht seasons in the Med, Red Sea and polar expeditions
intro: Scenic and its confirmed sister brand Emerald Cruises bring true all-inclusive luxury to rivers and oceans alike, with a genuine Red Sea and Seychelles season for GCC-region clients.
description: Scenic Luxury Cruises & Tours (ultra-luxury river 'Space-Ships' and the expedition yacht Scenic Eclipse) and Emerald Cruises (deluxe river 'Star-Ships' and boutique ocean yachts) sit inside the same corporate group and share a loyalty programme, Scenic and Emerald Rewards. Both brands price all-inclusive: fares, excursions, drinks and gratuities are bundled from the outset, which makes quoting simple and the final invoice easy to explain to clients.

For GCC-region clients, Emerald's ocean yachts run a Red Sea season (Aqaba, Jeddah, Safaga, Sharm El Sheikh) and a Seychelles & Indian Ocean season (ex-Mahé), the two most geographically relevant products in either brand's worldwide network. We wholesale allocation across both brands' river and ocean programmes for agents building premium, higher-end itineraries.

A genuine Red Sea season (Emerald Azzurra/Sakara) ex-Aqaba and Jeddah
River sailings across Europe and the Mekong alongside true polar expedition voyages on Scenic Eclipse
A 'good–better' pairing for clients within one relationship and one loyalty programme

faqs.q: What do Scenic and Emerald offer closest to the GCC?
faqs.a: Emerald is the regional brand of the pair: its yachts run a Red Sea season calling Jeddah, Aqaba and Sharm El Sheikh, and a Seychelles & Indian Ocean season from Mahé — both a short flight from the Gulf. Scenic adds European river cruising and polar expeditions as fly-cruises.

faqs.q: What's the difference between Scenic and Emerald?
faqs.a: Scenic sits at the ultra-luxury end — smaller guest counts, higher space ratios, and premium extras such as helicopters and a submersible on Scenic Eclipse. Emerald offers a more accessible deluxe/boutique-yacht tier under the same parent group, so clients can be offered a 'good–better' pairing within one relationship.

faqs.q: Are the fares genuinely all-inclusive?
faqs.a: Yes — both brands bundle port charges, meals, most beverages, Wi-Fi and gratuities into the headline fare, and Emerald's yachts add an included daily shore excursion.

faqs.q: Can we offer clients a Nile or Egypt river cruise under these brands?
faqs.a: No — neither Scenic nor Emerald currently list an Egypt/Nile river product on their official sites; this should not be offered on the strength of either brand.

faqs.q: Is there a shared loyalty programme?
faqs.a: Yes, Scenic and Emerald Rewards spans both brands.

faqs.q: What's the best season for a Red Sea sailing?
faqs.a: Emerald's Red Sea itineraries run across the 2026/27 season ex-Aqaba and Jeddah — confirm the specific voyage dates directly with us before quoting.

A third ship, Crystal Grace, joins in 2028 and is already on sale across Europe and the Americas.

Dubai is a genuine turnaround port for Crystal Symphony, not just a port of call: spring sailings run Dubai–Jeddah, Dubai–Barcelona and Dubai–Fort Lauderdale, plus a Singapore–Dubai repositioning voyage calling at the Musandam Peninsula (Oman) and Abu Dhabi along the way. name: Aroya Cruises
signature: Red Sea short breaks of 2–8 nights from Jeddah and a summer Mediterranean season from Istanbul
intro: AROYA is Saudi Arabia's homegrown cruise line — a single 335-metre ship sailing the Red Sea from Jeddah and the Mediterranean from Istanbul, with a distinctly Arabian welcome built in from the start.
description: AROYA Cruises, owned by Cruise Saudi (Public Investment Fund), operates one ship — simply 'Aroya' — carrying up to 3,362 guests across 18 decks. Its Red Sea season, branded 'Red Coral Secrets,' runs September to May from Jeddah, calling at ports across Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Jordan; the ship repositions each summer to Istanbul for a Mediterranean season via the Suez Canal. Onboard, the line is built around family and faith-conscious features: a nursery, a large Kid Zone and water park, women-only pool/spa/gym hours, separate prayer rooms and shisha lounges.

AROYA is the closest thing the region has to a home-market cruise line — Saudi-owned, and sailing the Red Sea from Jeddah plus a Mediterranean season from Istanbul, both a short flight from any GCC city. As Preferred Sales Agent we carry direct fares and cabin holds across both seasons, and we will tell you first as new departure ports are released.

faqs.q: Where does AROYA sail from?
faqs.a: Jeddah for the Red Sea and Istanbul for the Mediterranean — the two home ports on sale. Jeddah is a short direct hop from every GCC city, which makes AROYA the closest cruise product to this market: Red Sea round trips of two to eight nights calling Sharm El Sheikh, Aqaba, Yanbu and Jabal Al-Sabaya, plus a summer Mediterranean season from Istanbul.

faqs.q: What documents do clients need for a Jeddah round trip?
faqs.a: For round-trip Red Sea sailings that start and end in Jeddah with no international port calls, a KSA National ID or Iqama is sufficient. A passport is required for itineraries with international calls, and residents should ensure any exit/re-entry visas are valid.

faqs.q: Is AROYA suitable for families?
faqs.a: Yes — the ship has a dedicated nursery for ages 6–24 months, a large Kid Zone and water park, and a Premier Family Suite category.

faqs.q: Are there women-only facilities onboard?
faqs.a: Yes — exclusive pool, spa and gym hours for women are offered (published hours vary by itinerary), alongside separate male and female prayer rooms.

faqs.q: Does AROYA support AED bookings?
faqs.a: Yes — the booking engine's currency selector includes AED alongside SAR, USD, EUR and GBP.

faqs.q: How big is the ship?
faqs.a: 335 metres long, 18 decks, 1,678 cabins, with a maximum capacity of 3,362 guests and over 1,600 crew.

intro: Carnival's easy-going, value-led approach makes it a dependable fly-cruise recommendation for GCC families — 1,667 departures on sale for July 2026 – July 2027, every one starting with a flight to the US, Australia or a seasonal European home port.
description: Carnival Cruise Line operates around 32 ships across the Caribbean, the Bahamas (including its new private destination Celebration Key), Mexico's west coast, Alaska and a growing Australia deployment. Its Excel-class flagships — Mardi Gras, Carnival Celebration and Carnival Jubilee — are LNG-powered and built around big family attractions such as the BOLT® rollercoaster and multi-slide Carnival WaterWorks™ water parks, paired on the same ship with an adults-only Serenity Retreat and celebrity-chef dining from Emeril Lagasse and Guy Fieri.

Carnival sells to the GCC as a fly-cruise, across 28 home ports: the Caribbean and Bahamas from Miami, Orlando (Port Canaveral), Galveston, Tampa and New Orleans; Alaska from Seattle; Australia and the South Pacific from Sydney and Brisbane; a summer Europe season from London, Barcelona, Rome and Lisbon; and Asia from Singapore, Hong Kong and Tokyo. faqs.q: Which Carnival home port suits a GCC client best?
faqs.a: Singapore and Hong Kong are the shortest hops from the Gulf, and Carnival home-ports both. For the classic Carnival holiday, sell the Caribbean or Bahamas out of Miami or Orlando (Port Canaveral) — that is where the newest Excel-class ships and Celebration Key sit. Europe from London, Barcelona or Rome works well as a summer alternative.

faqs.q: What is Celebration Key?
faqs.a: Carnival's newest private destination on Grand Bahama Island, with five themed zones: Paradise Plaza, the family-focused Starfish Lagoon, the adults' Calypso Lagoon, the adults-only Pearl Cove Beach Club, and Lokono Cove for Bahamian culture — plus a mile-long beach.

faqs.q: Which ships suit a first-time GCC family booking?
faqs.a: The Excel-class ships — Mardi Gras, Carnival Celebration and Carnival Jubilee — pair the BOLT® rollercoaster and large-format Carnival WaterWorks™ water parks with a Serenity Adult-Only Retreat, so families and couples can share the same sailing comfortably.

faqs.q: What travel documents do GCC clients need?
faqs.a: Carnival's own Help hub maintains a distinct 'Non-U.S. Citizens' guidance track, separate from US-citizen instructions — we point clients to this directly rather than the American documentation.

faqs.q: Is Australia a realistic option for GCC clients?
faqs.a: Yes — it's the one major non-US home-porting market Carnival sells at scale, with year-round departures from Sydney and Brisbane. It's still a long-haul flight from the Gulf, but it avoids US visa/ESTA processing for clients who prefer that.

faqs.q: Can a Carnival cruise be combined with a US or Australia stay?
faqs.a: Yes — since every Carnival sailing requires a flight from the Gulf, we typically build a Miami, Orlando or Sydney city stay either side of the cruise into the same booking.

name: StarDream Cruises
tagline: Asia's own cruise group — Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Japan
signature: Short 2–5 night Asia sailings from Singapore and Hong Kong, plus Taiwan–Japan–Korea voyages
intro: StarDream Cruises is the umbrella that now carries Asia's best-known cruise heritage — Dream Cruises and StarCruises, the successors to the Genting cruise fleet and the brief Resorts World Cruises relaunch — sailing Singapore, Hong Kong and a Taiwan/Japan/Korea season for GCC clients wanting an Asia fly-cruise.
description: StarDream Cruises, launched in March 2025, is the current legal successor to Resorts World Cruises, itself the post-pandemic relaunch of the original Genting Hong Kong / Star Cruises fleet. Genting Dream also carries genuine Muslim-friendly certification — certified Halal cuisine, Jain vegetarian options and a HalalTrip Gastronomy Awards partnership — that travels well with GCC clientele.

StarDream is a short-break Asia specialist, and it sells actively into this market — the group runs UAE, Oman and Qatar market sites of its own. We wholesale allocation across Genting Dream from Singapore, Star Voyager from Hong Kong and Malaysia, and Star Navigator from Keelung into Japan and South Korea, so you can build a two- to five-night Asia fly-cruise around a Singapore or Hong Kong stay. Deployments move between seasons under this group — check the current ship and home port with us before you quote.

faqs.q: Which ship is best for a luxury family booking?

faqs.q: What's the difference between Dream Cruises and StarCruises?

faqs.q: How would a GCC client best combine this with a cruise?
faqs.a: As an Asia fly-cruise: Singapore (Genting Dream, year-round) and Hong Kong (Star Voyager, seasonal) are both well served by direct long-haul flights from Gulf hubs, and pair naturally with a city stay either side of the sailing.
